description: Check bullion sales tax rules by state. Compare exemptions and rates for gold and silver purchases to plan your order with confidence.
text:
Sales Tax Guide for Shoppers
Will You Pay Sales Tax? Find Your State
Sales tax on bullion, coins, and jewelry varies by state. Pick yours below for a plain-English summary of what gets taxed, what doesn't, and when.
The quick basics
Investment bullion
— gold/silver/platinum bars, rounds, and coins priced on metal content. Tax-free in most states.
Collector / numismatic coins
— rare or graded coins priced on rarity. Usually taxed.
Jewelry & accessories
— always taxed like other goods, even when made of precious metal.
Some states have a minimum
— in NY, CA, CT, MA, and VA, your order has to clear a dollar threshold to qualify for the exemption.

New York
In New York, qualifying bullion and coin orders are tax-free if your order total is at least $1,000. Smaller orders, jewelry, and collectibles are taxed normally.

California
In California, qualifying bullion and coin orders are tax-free if your order total is at least $2,000. Smaller orders, jewelry, and collectibles are taxed normally.

Florida
In Florida, sales tax depends on what you buy and how it qualifies. Some items are exempt; others are taxed.

Washington
In Washington, sales tax applies to bullion, coins, jewelry, and accessories — just like other goods.

New Hampshire
New Hampshire has no state sales tax. You won't see any sales tax on your order.

Alaska
Alaska has no state sales tax. Some local boroughs and cities collect their own tax, so the amount you pay depends on your delivery address.
